# protobuf-nio

> Java library (Java 25+) for sending and receiving Protocol Buffers messages over TCP between Java applications. Each connection is a blocking socket served by two virtual threads; no Netty, no framework. Dependencies: protobuf-java 4.x and slf4j-api 2.x. API package: `io.github.quantranuk.protobuf.nio`.

## Install

Maven coordinates: `io.github.quantranuk:protobuf-nio-core:2.0.0` (Maven Central). Requires Java 25 or later.

## Complete example

`Ping` and `Pong` stand for any classes generated by protoc from your `.proto` file (here with a `string text` field).

```java
import io.github.quantranuk.protobuf.nio.ProtoClient;
import io.github.quantranuk.protobuf.nio.ProtoServer;

public class Example {
    public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception {
        ProtoServer server = ProtoServer.builder(3456)
                .onMessage(Ping.class, (connection, ping) -> connection.send(Pong.newBuilder().setText("pong").build()))
                .build();
        server.start();

        ProtoClient client = ProtoClient.builder("localhost", 3456)
                .onMessage(Pong.class, (c, pong) -> System.out.println(pong.getText()))
                .onDisconnected((c, reason, cause) -> System.out.println("closed: " + reason))
                .build();
        client.connect();                                   // throws IOException if it can't connect
        client.send(Ping.newBuilder().setText("ping").build());

        Thread.sleep(500);                                  // a real program would wait for the reply
        client.close();                                     // graceful: writes what's queued, then closes
        server.close();
    }
}
```

## API at a glance

- `ProtoServer.builder(port)` / `ProtoClient.builder(host, port)`: settings and callbacks, then `build()`. Builders are reusable.
- Callbacks on both builders: `onConnected`, `onMessage(Type.class, handler)`, `onOtherMessage`, `onRawMessage(Type.class, handler)`, `onSendFailure`, `onDisconnected`. On a server they receive the `ProtoConnection`; on a client, the `ProtoClient`.
- `server.start()`, `server.broadcast(message)`, `server.broadcast(message, filter)`, `server.connections()`, `server.close()`.
- `client.connect()` (or `connectAsync()`), `client.send(message)`, `client.close()`, `client.awaitClosed()`.
- `connection.send(message)`, `connection.close()`, `connection.server()` (to broadcast from a callback), `connection.attach(state)` / `connection.attachment()` (returns `Object`).
- Settings include `readTimeout`, `heartbeatInterval`, `writeTimeout`, `closeTimeout`, `maxMessageSize`, `maxPendingMessages`, `maxPendingBytes`, `overflowPolicy` (`BLOCK`, `REJECT`, `DROP_OLDEST`, `DISCONNECT`), `tls(SSLContext)`, `allowOnlyHandledTypes()` or `allowedMessageTypes(...)`, and on the server `maxConnections`. For every `Duration` setting, `Duration.ZERO` means no limit.

## Rules that are easy to get wrong

1. **Callbacks for different connections run concurrently.** Each connection has its own reader thread, so state shared by a server's callbacks (or by clients built from one builder) must be thread-safe. One connection's callbacks run in order, never at the same time, and may block: that stalls only that connection.
2. **A `ProtoClient` is single-use.** After it closes, for any reason, it can't connect again: build a new one from the same builder. Calling `connect()` twice throws `IllegalStateException`.
3. **Both peers need the same generated classes.** Messages are identified on the wire by their Java class name, so both sides must be Java, and renaming or moving a message class breaks compatibility with peers that still use the old one.
4. **`onMessage(Type.class, ...)` matches the exact class, once.** Registering a second handler for the same type throws `IllegalArgumentException`. Messages of other types go to `onOtherMessage`, or are logged at WARN once per type and dropped.
5. **`send` returning `false` has already been reported.** When the queue is full, `onSendFailure` with reason `REJECTED` has run before `send` returns; don't report it again. With the default `BLOCK` policy, `send` waits up to `sendTimeout` for room. Once closing has started, `send` returns `false` without any callback.
6. **A failed `connect()` calls no callback.** It throws an `IOException` instead (`java.net.ProtocolException` if the peer isn't protobuf-nio, which retrying won't fix). `onDisconnected` only follows a successful connect, and it's always the last callback, exactly once.
7. **On the module path**, export your generated package to the library: `exports com.example.proto to io.github.quantranuk.protobuf.nio;`. Otherwise receiving those messages fails with an error naming that line.
8. **`close()` is graceful and blocks** until queued messages are written and the peer has closed, within `closeTimeout` (5 s by default).
9. **`build()` rejects contradictions**: a type with both `onMessage` and `onRawMessage`, a handled type missing from `allowedMessageTypes`, or `allowOnlyHandledTypes()` with no handler, with `onOtherMessage` or with `allowedMessageTypes`. Use `allowOnlyHandledTypes()` for untrusted peers.
10. **A callback can't use the server variable it's being built into** (`server` isn't assigned yet): use `connection.server()`.

## Documentation

- [README](https://github.com/quantranuk/protobuf-nio#readme): overview, comparison with gRPC and Netty, performance
- [Callbacks and threads](https://github.com/quantranuk/protobuf-nio#callbacks-and-threads): the threading contract
- [Sending and backpressure](https://github.com/quantranuk/protobuf-nio#sending-and-backpressure): queues and overflow policies
- [Configuration](https://github.com/quantranuk/protobuf-nio#configuration): every setting and its default
- [Hardening checklist](https://github.com/quantranuk/protobuf-nio#hardening-checklist): settings for untrusted networks
- [TLS](https://github.com/quantranuk/protobuf-nio#tls), [Raw handlers](https://github.com/quantranuk/protobuf-nio#raw-handlers), [Wire format](https://github.com/quantranuk/protobuf-nio#wire-format)
- Javadoc: in the published `-javadoc.jar`, and in the sources of `ProtoServer`, `ProtoClient` and `ProtoConnection`
